summary.text: A man with a past history of alcohol-related fatty liver and a smoking history presented to the emergency department with two months of generalized weakness, abdominal pain, increased thirst with urinary frequency, constipation and difficulty sleeping. Examination showed hepatomegaly with otherwise normal vital signs, and admission laboratory testing showed elevated calcium with high PTHrP and low intact PTH.

CT of the abdomen and pelvis showed a large complex multifocal liver mass with mild intrahepatic bile duct dilatation. He was admitted and treated with intravenous fluids, calcitonin and zoledronic acid. PET-CT showed hypermetabolic liver activity, upper abdominal lymph nodes, omental/peritoneal activity, ascites and small pulmonary nodules, suspicious for metastatic disease.

CT-guided liver biopsy showed poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma with squamous features, positive for CEA, CK19, P63 and CK5/6, and the diagnosis of adenosquamous cholangiocarcinoma was made. Humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy was diagnosed on the basis of PTHrP. Cisplatin and gemcitabine chemotherapy was started after the diagnosis was confirmed.

The course was marked by recurrent admissions with worsening symptoms and uncontrolled hypercalcemia, complicated by acute kidney injury, cholestatic hyperbilirubinemia and pancreatitis, with percutaneous transhepatic cholecystostomy required. His condition further deteriorated and he died within three months of diagnosis.
